objective: Frozen computation: on the not-all-equal thread, a chain of knots sharing one distinction, the six-regular weave (L = 6, 9, 12) and a threshold-line control, test whether the differ count is built from unit steps (P1), skips no level from any start (P2), and what order betweenness gives from a start; bond distance and steps apart as references; exploratory census of all not-all-equal relations at n <= 6.
status: Supported 2026-11-17 (refereed R1, every number recomputed): 9 of 9 frozen predictions held: under exact additive betweenness no distinction lies between two others on the thread, a chain of 15 knots and the weave (L = 6, 9, 12, exact); with flips chain 4 (3 without the start's flip); tau = steps apart on the chain only; weave rate 2/3 at one step, below 1/2 at every third distinction of a row; census betweenness 0 / 732 / 87,924 at n = 4, 5, 6. Referee: read only as order the weave start has 12 nearest neighbours; non-constant P1 is 72 / 780 by the natural definition.
title: Does the differ count give an order with nothing skipped
